items.text: They check in when they're running late.
They go through your phone 'just to see'.
items.why: Checking your phone without permission is a control and trust issue, not affection.

items.text: They want you to meet their friends after a few months.

items.why: If every past relationship is someone else's fault, notice whether they ever take responsibility.

items.text: They love a spreadsheet for holiday planning.
items.why: Beige flags are quirks: not good or bad, just them.

items.text: They apologise and change the behaviour.
They say 'I love you' on date two and want to move in.
items.why: Intense, fast commitment early on can be love bombing. Healthy closeness builds over time.

items.text: They respect it when you say you're busy.
They sulk for days instead of talking.
items.why: Long silent treatment punishes rather than resolves.

items.text: They narrate what their cat is thinking.
They pressure you to skip plans with friends.
items.why: Isolating you from friends is a classic warning sign.

items.text: They take ages to reply but always reply properly.
They remember things you told them weeks ago.
